sections.html: Amatitlania sajica can become up to 12 cm in the male sex and up to 9 cm in the female, and is regarded as one of the smallest species of the genus.
Amatitlania sajica comes from the Pacific side of Costa Rica.

Most Central American cichlids, earlier grouped in the collective genus Cichlasoma, are kept by experienced aquarists who prefer a big aquarium with few, characterful fishes. They do not make compromises and show complex and varied behaviour.

Some relatively peaceful and comparatively small species show the exciting behaviour of their bigger and rougher cousins, but can also be kept in a well chosen community of other fish, such as catfish, barbs, tetras and livebearers, especially as they treat plants rather gently. A. sajica is among these species.

These cichlids have not been imported for a long time; all specimens in the hobby are bred ones. They are productive open breeders. The sight of such a pair leading their young has often turned community tank aquarists into breeders.
